title: On Cross-Dataset Generalization in Automatic Detection of Online Abuse

bias_targets.methodology: Used unsupervised topic modeling (Latent Dirichlet Allocation) to extract and categorize topics from the training dataset. Evaluated how the distribution of domain-specific versus general/identity-related topics impacts a BERT classifier's cross-dataset generalization on out-of-domain offensive language datasets.

Trained a toxicity classifier on a dataset with a broad, general definition of toxicity (Wikipedia Detox) and measured its zero-shot generalization performance on out-of-domain test sets annotated with different, specific definitions of abuse, such as sexism, racism, and hate speech.

Re-sampled the training dataset to create subsets with varying ratios of toxic to normal instances (e.g., balanced 1:1 vs. imbalanced 1:10) and measured the resulting trade-off between True Positive and True Negative rates on out-of-domain evaluation datasets.
